text:
RECOMMENDATION: DON'T RAISE IT
LIKELIHOOD: 15

Panel composition on its own is close to meaningless. Four women can easily arise by chance, especially as HR and senior-management panels in banking often skew female even where the technical workforce doesn't. Raising it as your opening argument signals grievance rather than evidence, and tends to harden the other side.

Also, your credentials aren't obviously superior for this role. "Head of risk modelling" is a leadership and regulator-facing job; a panel can legitimately rate regulatory fluency and stakeholder credibility above a PhD and deeper technical depth.

The real issue is the ignored request. Chase it in writing, cite any internal policy on feedback timelines, and ask for the scoring criteria. Judge by what comes back.
